content: 1. Erythromycin lactobionate and fluphenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 2. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of fondaparinux by reducing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 3. Erythromycin lactobionate and formoterol both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 4. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Fosamprenavir also increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate via the same mechanism. This combination is contraindicated. 5. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and erythromycin lactobionate reciprocally increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 7. Erythromycin lactobionate and gemifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 8. Erythromycin lactobionate and gilteritinib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 9. Erythromycin lactobionate and givinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs at initiation, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is a change from baseline greater than 60 ms. 10. Erythromycin lactobionate and glasdegib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for increased risk of QTc prolongation. 11. Erythromycin lactobionate and granisetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 12. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 14. Erythromycin lactobionate and haloperidol both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 15. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of heparin by reducing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 16. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while hydrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate via the same mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 17. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 18. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 19. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor; avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. 20. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of iloperidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of imipramine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Imipramine and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 22. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and indinavir reciprocally increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 23. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of infigratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 24. Inotuzumab and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs and monitor electrolytes before and after initiation of any QTc-prolonging drug, and periodically monitor as clinically indicated. 25. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of irinotecan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of irinotecan liposomal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 27. Isoflurane and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 28. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 29. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Itraconazole and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 30. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of ivabradine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of ivabradine with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 31. Ivosidenib and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of QTc-prolonging drugs with ivosidenib or replace with alternative therapies. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor patients for loss of therapeutic effect. 32. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 33. Erythromycin lactobionate and ketoconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 34. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and lapatinib reciprocally increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate. This combination is contraindicated. 35. Lasmiditan increases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 36. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 37. Leniolisib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transporters. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 38. Erythromycin lactobionate and levoketoconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 39. Lithium and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 40. Lofepramine and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 41. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and lopinavir reciprocally increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 42. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of loratadine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 43. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 44. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin lactobionate and lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate. This combination is contraindicated. 45. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 46. Macimorelin and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Macimorelin increases the QTc interval by approximately 11 ms. Avoid coadministration with QT-prolonging drugs to reduce the risk of torsade de pointes. Allow sufficient washout time of QT-prolonging drugs before administering macimorelin. 47. Maprotiline and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 48. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 49. Marijuana increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 50. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of mestranol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 51. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of methadone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 52. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while methylprednisolone decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 53. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 54. Miconazole vaginal increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 55. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of microbiota oral therapy due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating microbiota oral therapy. 56. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of midazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 57. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of intranasal midazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors with intranasal midazolam increases systemic exposure, potentially prolonging sedation. 58. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 59. Mirtazapine and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 60. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of mizolastine by reducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 61. Erythromycin lactobionate and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 62. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 63. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of naloxegol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 64. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 65. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and nelfinavir reciprocally increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 66. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of neratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of neratinib with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 67. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 68. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of nicardipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 69. Nifedipine increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 70. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and nilotinib reciprocally increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 71. Nilutamide increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 72. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of nintedanib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If adverse effects occur, management may require dose reduction, therapy interruption, or discontinuation. 73. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of nirogacestat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 74. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of nisoldipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 75. Nortriptyline and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 76. Erythromycin lactobionate and octreotide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 77. Olanzapine and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 78. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of olaparib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, monitor closely.
